name: AND Gate
description: Add an AND gate using the button on the toolbar, drag it to the correct position, then connect the start nodes (left) to it and the end node (right), using the connection tool ✏️.
commentCorrect: Nice! Well done on completing the first level. To recap: The AND gate requires two inputs, that both must be TRUE to give a TRUE output.
commentWrong: Unfortunately this doesn't look right. Remember the AND gate needs two inputs, and gives one output which is TRUE when both inputs are TRUE
commentHint: Plop an AND gate from the toolbar, then connect the start nodes to it and the end node, using the connection tool ✏️

name: AND Gate
description: What about when we don't have a TRUE value as an input?
commentCorrect: So any FALSE input will give a FALSE output from an AND gate. Lets test this on the next level.
commentWrong: That doesn't look right. In this exercise we are looking to connect everything up like the previous level, but with one FALSE input.
commentHint: Drag an AND gate from the toolbar, then connect the start nodes to it and the end node, using the connection tool ✏️

name: AND Gate
description: Try to make one AND gate that outputs a TRUE value, and one that outputs FALSE.
commentCorrect: Correct! Looks like you are getting the hang of this!
commentWrong: Not quite - this level you need to have one output that is FALSE and one that is TRUE.
commentHint: Two gates are needed here, with two different input combinations to give one FALSE and one TRUE output.

name: AND Gate
description: What is the expected output from this circuit?
commentCorrect: Well done, yes the output would indeed be TRUE.
commentWrong: Sorry no, that doesn't look correct.
commentHint: Remember, and AND gate takes two TRUE inputs and returns TRUE, anything else will result in FALSE being returned.

name: AND Gate
description: What about the expected output from this circuit?
commentCorrect: Well done, yes the output would indeed be FALSE.
commentWrong: Sorry no, that doesn't look correct.
commentHint: Remember, and AND gate takes two TRUE inputs and returns TRUE, anything else will result in FALSE being returned.

name: OR Gate
description: Use the OR gate that outputs TRUE when one input is TRUE, and FALSE for the other times.
commentCorrect: Correct! An OR gate outputs TRUE when either input, or both inputs are TRUE
commentWrong: Not quite. Are you sure you connected everything correctly?
commentHint: Place one OR gate between the two start nodes (left) and the end node (right), and connect the gate to the nodes.

name: OR Gate
description: What happens when neither input is true? Complete the level to find out.
commentCorrect: Correct! An OR gate outputs FALSE when either input, or both inputs are FALSE
commentWrong: Not quite. Are you sure you connected everything correctly?
commentHint: Place one OR gate between the two start nodes (left) and the end node (right), and connect the gate to the nodes.

name: OR Gate
description: Using Three OR gates, make two outputs TRUE and the other FALSE.
commentCorrect: Correct! Good problem solving skills!
commentWrong: Not quite. 2 gates need to output TRUE, one needs to output FALSE.
commentHint: Remember that a OR gate will be TRUE if only one of its inputs is TRUE.

name: OR Gate
description: What is the expected output from this circuit?
commentCorrect: Well done! The final output is TRUE. Even though the first OR gate outputs FALSE, the second outputs TRUE, so the final OR gate also outputs TRUE.
commentWrong: Sorry, that's not correct. Try working through the circuit one OR gate at a time.
commentHint: Work from left to right. Calculate the output of the first two OR gates, then use those values as the inputs to the final OR gate.

name: OR Gate
description: What about the expected output from this circuit?
commentCorrect: Correct! Every input is FALSE, so both first-stage OR gates output FALSE. FALSE OR FALSE then gives a final output of FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Remember that an OR gate only outputs TRUE when at least one of its inputs is TRUE.
commentHint: Start with the two OR gates on the left. Both receive two FALSE values. What will each output? Then combine those results.

name: NOT Gate
description: A NOT gate reverses its input. Use two NOT gates to turn the TRUE input into FALSE, and the FALSE input into TRUE.
commentCorrect: Correct! A NOT gate simply reverses its input: TRUE becomes FALSE, and FALSE becomes TRUE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Each input should pass through a NOT gate, reversing its value.
commentHint: Connect each start node to its own NOT gate, then connect each NOT gate to an end node.

name: NOT & AND
description: NOT gates can change the values being sent into other gates. Use a NOT gate and an AND gate to produce a FALSE output from these two TRUE inputs.
commentCorrect: Correct!
commentWrong: Not quite. Both gates need to be used. Think about how changing one TRUE input with NOT will affect the AND gate.
commentHint: Pass one of the TRUE inputs through NOT before connecting it to the AND gate. Connect the other TRUE input directly to AND.

name: NOT and OR
description: Now try combining NOT with OR. Use a NOT gate and an OR gate to produce a TRUE output from these two FALSE inputs.
commentCorrect: Well done! Lets see how this works when we put it all togethr in the next level
commentWrong: Not quite. Try again!
commentHint: Pass one FALSE input through NOT, then use that result and the other FALSE input as the two inputs to OR.

name: NOT Gate
description: What is the expected output from this circuit? Work through each gate from left to right.
commentCorrect: Correct! TRUE becomes FALSE after NOT. FALSE AND FALSE gives FALSE, then FALSE OR TRUE gives a final output of TRUE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Try calculating the output from each gate in order, beginning with the NOT gate.
commentHint: Start with the TRUE input entering NOT. Use its output as one input to AND, then use the AND output as one input to OR.

name: NOT Gate
description: Make the output TRUE. You must use one of the NOT, AND and OR gates.
commentCorrect: Excellent!
commentWrong: Not quite. Make sure you are using all the gates and they are connected correctly.
commentHint: Start by connecting A and B to OR. Pass the OR output through NOT. Finally, connect the NOT output and C to AND.

name: NAND Gate
description: A NAND gate gives the opposite output to an AND gate. The first circuit uses an AND gate followed by NOT. Add a NAND gate to the second pair of inputs and make its output match the first circuit.
commentCorrect: Correct! The NAND gate produces exactly the same result as passing the output of an AND gate through NOT. NAND literally means NOT AND.
commentWrong: Not quite. The NAND circuit should give the same output as the AND gate followed by NOT.
commentHint: Connect the second pair of TRUE inputs to a NAND gate, then connect the NAND gate to the remaining end node.

name: NAND Gate
description: Now try using NAND on its own. Connect these inputs through a NAND gate to produce the correct output.
commentCorrect: Correct! TRUE AND FALSE would give FALSE, but NAND reverses the AND result, giving TRUE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Remember that NAND gives the opposite result to AND.
commentHint: Connect both inputs to one NAND gate. Ask yourself what AND would output first, then reverse it.

name: NAND Gate
description: What is the expected output from this NAND circuit?
commentCorrect: Correct! The first NAND receives TRUE and TRUE, so it outputs FALSE. The second NAND receives FALSE and TRUE, so the final output is TRUE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Work through the two NAND gates one at a time.
commentHint: The first NAND receives two TRUE inputs. Calculate its output first, then use that result as an input to the second NAND.

name: NAND Gate
description: This NAND circuit is more complicated. Work through each part of the circuit and determine the final output.
commentCorrect: Correct! The three NAND gates on the left produce FALSE, TRUE and TRUE. The next NAND therefore produces TRUE, leaving the final NAND with TRUE and TRUE, which gives FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. With a circuit this size, trying to calculate everything at once can get confusing. Work from left to right.
commentHint: Start with the three NAND gates on the left. Their outputs are then used as the inputs to the remaining two gates.

name: NAND Gate
description: Use all four gates available to build a circuit that produces a FALSE output. There may be more than one way to solve this level.
commentCorrect: Excellent! You have built a circuit using all four gate types learnt so far. A OR B gives TRUE. NOT C gives TRUE. TRUE AND D gives TRUE, and finally TRUE NAND TRUE gives FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Break the expression into smaller parts rather than trying to build the whole circuit at once.
commentHint: Start with the brackets. First build A OR B. Separately, pass C through NOT and combine that result with D using AND. The outputs of those two sections should become the inputs to NAND.

name: NOR Gate
description: A NOR gate gives the opposite output to an OR gate. The first circuit uses an OR gate followed by NOT. Add a NOR gate to the second pair of inputs and make its output match the first circuit.
commentCorrect: Correct! A NOR gate produces exactly the same result as passing the output of an OR gate through NOT. NOR literally means NOT OR.
commentWrong: Not quite. The NOR circuit should produce the same output as the OR gate followed by NOT.
commentHint: Connect the second pair of FALSE inputs to a NOR gate, then connect the NOR gate to the remaining end node.

name: NOR Gate
description: Use both a NOR gate and an AND gate to build a circuit that produces a TRUE output.
commentCorrect: Correct! You've combined a NOR gate with an AND gate to produce the required TRUE output.
commentWrong: Not quite. Your final output needs to be TRUE and both the NOR and AND gates need to be part of the circuit.
commentHint: Think about what a NOR gate does with two FALSE inputs. Its output could then be useful as an input to the AND gate.

name: NOR Gate
description: What is the expected output from this NOR gate?
commentCorrect: Correct! TRUE OR FALSE would produce TRUE, so NOR reverses that result and produces FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Remember that NOR gives the opposite result to OR.
commentHint: Work out TRUE OR FALSE first, then reverse the answer.

name: NOR Gate
description: This circuit contains three NOR gates. Work through it from left to right and determine the final output.
commentCorrect: Correct! The upper NOR receives FALSE and FALSE, so outputs TRUE. The lower NOR receives FALSE and TRUE, so outputs FALSE. The final NOR therefore receives TRUE and FALSE, giving FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Calculate the two NOR gates on the left before considering the final gate.
commentHint: The upper NOR outputs TRUE. The lower NOR outputs FALSE. Now apply NOR once more to those two values.

name: NOR Gate
description: This circuit combines everything you've studied so far. Work through each section carefully and determine the final output.
commentCorrect: Correct! The first NOR outputs TRUE, the OR outputs TRUE and the NOT outputs FALSE. The AND therefore outputs TRUE, while the NAND outputs TRUE. The final NOR receives TRUE and TRUE, producing FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. This circuit is easier if you calculate each layer separately rather than trying to follow the entire circuit at once.
commentHint: Start with the three gates on the left. Their outputs are TRUE, TRUE and FALSE. Use those values to calculate the AND and NAND gates before moving to the final NOR.

name: XOR Gate
description: XOR means Exclusive OR. Each gate below has one of the four possible input combinations. Connect each XOR gate to an end node and see how XOR behaves.
commentCorrect: Correct! XOR outputs FALSE when its inputs are the same, and TRUE when its inputs are different. So TRUE/TRUE gives FALSE, TRUE/FALSE gives TRUE, FALSE/TRUE gives TRUE and FALSE/FALSE gives FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Make sure each XOR gate is connected to an end node.
commentHint: Each XOR gate already has its two inputs. You only need to connect each gate's output to an end node.

name: XOR Gate
description: Use all four gates available to build a circuit that produces a TRUE output. There may be more than one solution.
commentCorrect: Correct! You used XOR together with AND, OR and NOT to produce the required TRUE output.
commentWrong: Not quite. Your circuit must produce TRUE and use all four available gatesd.
commentHint: Try producing two TRUE values before the final gate. For example, XOR can produce TRUE from different inputs, while OR followed by NOT can turn two FALSE inputs into TRUE.

name: XOR Gate
description: Use two XOR gates and the AND gate to build a circuit that produces a TRUE output. All three gates must be used, but there may be more than one solution.
commentCorrect: Excellent! You used two XOR gates and an AND gate together to produce TRUE.
commentWrong: Not quite. The final output needs to be TRUE, and both XOR gates and the AND gate must be used.
commentHint: Try using each XOR gate on a pair containing one TRUE and one FALSE. What outputs would that give? You could then combine those results with AND.

name: XOR Gate
description: What is the expected output from this XOR circuit?
commentCorrect: Correct! TRUE XOR FALSE gives TRUE. The second XOR therefore receives TRUE and TRUE, which gives FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Calculate the output of the first XOR gate before moving on to the second.
commentHint: The first XOR gate receives two different values, so it outputs TRUE. What does XOR do when both of its inputs are TRUE?

name: XOR Gate
description: This circuit combines XOR with some of the gates you've already seen. Work through each layer and determine the final output.
commentCorrect: Correct! The first XOR outputs TRUE, the AND outputs TRUE and the NOR outputs TRUE. TRUE XOR TRUE gives FALSE, while NOT TRUE gives FALSE. The final XOR therefore receives FALSE and FALSE, producing FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. This one has several stages, so calculate one layer at a time.
commentHint: Start with the three gates on the left. Their outputs are TRUE, TRUE and TRUE. Use those results to calculate the middle XOR and NOT gates before moving to the final XOR.

name: XNOR Gate
description: XNOR gives the opposite result to XOR. The first two circuits show XOR followed by NOT. Complete the final two circuits using XNOR and compare all four possible input combinations.
commentCorrect: Correct! XNOR gives exactly the same result as XOR followed by NOT. When both inputs are the same XNOR outputs TRUE, and when the inputs are different it outputs FALSE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Use the two XNOR gates to complete the remaining input combinations and compare their results with the XOR and NOT circuits above.
commentHint: Each remaining pair of inputs needs one XNOR gate. Connect FALSE and TRUE to one, and FALSE and FALSE to the other, then connect each gate to an end node.

name: XNOR Gate
description: Use the XNOR, OR and AND gates to build a circuit that produces a TRUE output. All three gates must be used, but there may be more than one solution.
commentCorrect: Correct! You successfully used XNOR together with OR and AND to produce TRUE.
commentWrong: Not quite. The final output must be TRUE and all three gates need to form part of the circuit.
commentHint: XNOR can produce TRUE from two matching inputs. Think about how you could combine that result with the remaining inputs using OR and AND.

name: XNOR Gate
description: This circuit combines XNOR with AND and OR. Work through each gate and determine the final output.
commentCorrect: Correct! Two TRUE values passed through a XNOR gate gives TRUE. FALSE AND TRUE gives FALSE. The final OR therefore receives TRUE and FALSE, giving TRUE.
commentWrong: Not quite. Calculate the XNOR and AND gates separately before moving to the final OR gate.
commentHint: The XNOR receives two matching values, while the AND gate receives FALSE and TRUE.

name: XNOR Gate
description: Build a circuit that produces a FALSE output using all five available gates. There may be more than one valid solution.
commentCorrect: Excellent! You used XNOR alongside several other gate types to construct a circuit with an FALSE output.
commentWrong: The final output needs to be FALSE and all five available gate types must be used in the completed circuit.
commentHint: Work backwards from the required FALSE output. Consider which gates can naturally produce FALSE, then use the remaining gates to create the input values they need.

name: XNOR Gate
description: This circuit combines several different gate types. Work through each layer carefully and determine the final output. Remember a gate with a small circle after the main shape is the NOT version of that gate.
commentCorrect: Correct! You successfully traced the complete mixed circuit and found the FALSE output.
commentWrong: Not quite. This circuit has several layers, so calculate each pair of gates before moving further to the right.
commentHint: Start with the four gates on the left. Their outputs are TRUE, TRUE, TRUE and FALSE. Use those results to calculate the OR and NAND gates, then continue towards the final XNOR.

name: SANDBOX
description: Try anything out
